desc: Reservation recommended.

name: La Coupole
desc: The famous Art Deco brasserie, convenient for a quick meal before or after a train journey to or from Montparnasse station.

name: Le Dôme
hours: Closed Su M in Jul and Aug

name: Le Duc
price: Set lunch €49, dinner a la carte €60-150
hours: Closed Su M, 3 weeks in Aug, 24 Dec-3 Jan

name: Les Grillades de Buenos Aires
desc: Small and intimate Argentinian restaurant. Amazing steaks. Everything about the food is wonderful.

name: Le Zeyer
desc: Famous Art Deco-style brasserie.

name: Le Lion Indomptable
desc: A small place that serves excellent Cameroonian and Senegalese food. The chef/waiter is a character and will keep you entertained.

name: Lou Pascalou
desc: Well hidden but worth seeking out, this unassuming restaurant serves happily inexpensive good food.

name: La Belle Villoise
desc: An underground, and thus hipper, alternative to La Maroquinerie next door.

name: Flèche d'Or
desc: An old train station which has been transformed into a hip, popular night club.

name: Gambetta
desc: All things Jamaican: reggae, dub, jazz, etc.

name: Goguette
desc: A mainly Latino-American club.

name: La Maroquinerie
desc: It's a bar/café/restaurant upstairs and a music club (mostly indi rock) downstairs. As of this writing the Maroquinerie is one of the most happening indie venues in Paris (along with the Fleche d'Or).

name: Nawab
desc: This Indian and Pakistani restaurant is usually packed especially for lunch so be sure to call ahead and reserve a table. One of the reasons is that if you ask them to spice it up "like in Pakistan" they actually will.

name: Le Surcouf
desc: Very ordinary non-touristy cafe run by family from the Maghreb. "French" food is pricey for what you get, but the couscous dishes are huge, cheap and delicious with a home-cooked feel to them. There's a dog hanging aroun

name: La Travesia
desc: Inexpensive but excellent Lebanese food. Vegetarian friendly. Just down the steps from the Sacre Coeur.

name: Au Grain de Folie
desc: A one-woman operation with some mixed reviews, but apparently when she gets it right it's just about the best dining experience you'll ever have. Booking a day ahead is suggested.

name: Le Buffet
desc: Tasty, homey French food in a family-run restaurant. Lunch menu is around €12 (can be had until 20ː00).

name: Cafe des Deux Moulins
desc: A popular destination for those who love the film Le fabuleaux destin d'Amelie Poulain, yet some locals still come here. Interior preserves the movie set. Great for lunch.

name: La Petaudiere
desc: Piano bar. Tasty food, nice ambience, and excellent good piano music (prepare some coins for the pianist).

name: Le Refuge des Fondues
desc: Fondue restaurant for young people: menu for €17, including wine served in a baby bottle, appetizers, the fondue itself (cheese or meat), and dessert.

name: La Taverne de Montmartre
desc: Small restaurant with a nice rustic decoration, just below the artist's square, place du Tertre. Relaxing place, not overloaded with tourists. Excellent fondue offered for €17 per person (Oct 2008), including a salami sa

name: Markotte
desc: Organic sandwiches, salads and soups

name: Le Basilic
desc: Very nice atmosphere and service. Great food, and good selection of wines.

name: Au Progres
desc: Small bar in an old place.

name: La Boule Noire
desc: A small venue which is decorated to resemble a 1920s speakeasy, which has hosted a range of musicians from local singers to major arena acts.

name: Le Divan du Monde
desc: A fairly major venue for indi-rock, hip-hop, and other concerts. The prices are usually pretty good and the size of the venue and decor are great.

name: Olympic Café
desc: Run as part of the Laboratoire Multi-culturel populaire the Olympic Café is one of the few places in Paris where you can reliably find avant-garde jazz, making it at least spiritually a descendant of the club where the A

name: Truc Café
desc: A classic French wine bistro filled with young trendy singles.

name: Au Boeuf Couronné
desc: Charming and laid-back, this restaurant has a somewhat old fashioned decor (think hard leather chairs, etc). As of May 2024, the food and the service are reported as no longer top-quality.

name: Café de la Musique
desc: Its varied selection of music is what draws the crowds here en masse, at any given night you're likely to hear soulful jazz tunes, or a hip DJ spinning robotic techno. Under chef Alain Podou's watch, the food here is sop

name: Rosa Bonheur
desc: This buvette near the south edge of the Parc des Buttes-Chaumont offers a range of tapas and drinks in a charming relaxed atmosphere. Hang out on a sunny day and watch the kids run around and play.

name: La Cascade
desc: Quiet bar that serves its beers cold and has an extensive wine list.

name: Péniche Anako
desc: Canal d'Ourcq barge, this one specializing in shows celebrating cultures from around the world.

name: Péniche Antipode
desc: A barge in the Canal d'Ourcq hosting magic acts and music.

name: Paname Brewing Company Tap House
desc: Tap house with 16 beers on tap and restaurant. Great views across along the Ourcq. Pizzas, burgers and salads available.

name: Choux d'enfer
addr: Intersection rue Jean Rey and quai Branly
desc: Street food + haute pâtisserie française = sweet food in a designer "kiosk".

name: Café Beaugrenelle
desc: Brasserie on lively Place Charles Michels

name: Le Café du Commerce
desc: Authentic French food and ambience. (Be sure to go to number 51 rue du Commerce, as there is another place nearby with a similar name.)

name: La Plage Parisienne
desc: Along the River, rather pleasant. They also offer cocktails at their bar.

name: Le Volant
desc: The Basque restaurant excels in meat. If you are lucky the soup of the day is the "soupe au marron". There is a possibility to get a 3-course evening menu including entrée, plat and dessert. The home-made "mousse au choc

name: Au Roi du café
desc: Belle-Epoque decor, true bisto spirit

name: Bermuda Onion
addr: Centre commercial Beaugrenelle, Ilôt Verseau - 3rd floor, 7 rue Linois
desc: Eat or drink. View of the river even better in the evening.

name: Eclectic
desc: Brasserie fashion. Decor Tom Dixon

name: Le Baribal
desc: 40-year-old neighborhood bistro run by Louisette and her partner George. Traditional simple fare.

name: Frame Brasserie
desc: Californian-style restaurant : a new take on the traditional Parisian brasserie.

name: Afaria
desc: This Basque restaurant mainly serves meat or some fancy tapas on the bar.

name: Le Beurre Noisette
desc: The restaurant of Thierry Bianqui offers interesting food all year long. Remember to reserve in advance for this cosy place. The menu are written on chalk boards and they can arrange custom demands for vegetarians. The d

name: Le Ciel de Paris
desc: 360° view.

name: Restaurant Benkay
addr: Hotel Novotel Front de Seine Grenelle, 61 quai de Grenelle
desc: Japanese cuisine. Great views.

name: Celtic Corner Pub
desc: A nice little Irish pub with charming service and fair price. Sports men from the nearby Gymnase "Croix Nivert" like to hang out here for a beer or two.

name: Crocodile Vert
desc: The small hidden Cuban bar is a bit away from rue de Vaugirard. It is quite popular for the salsa music on the weekends. At later times you'll recognise it by the number of people standing outside.

name: Le square café
desc: In spring time sun is shining on the outdoor terrace. It is a nice spot for a tea with soft background music.

name: Le César Palace Paris
desc: Diner and show - Parisian cabaret show and dancing.

name: Brasserie Wepler
desc: Excellent service, open late, seafood specialities. It is closed for renovations.

name: Restaurant Brigitte
desc: Finely prepared french cuisine served in a fancy bistrot environment. One of the notable point of this restaurant is their large collection of Chartreuse liquors.

name: A Jean Bart
desc: A typical Parisian brasserie, with all the classic food options. Croques monsieur are available at the counter.

name: Le Bar Belge
desc: Opened in 1954 as Paris was finally recovering from the occupation, the Bar Belge serves dozens of different Belgian beers, ales, and lambics in a locals-dominated, but very friendly room. They also have Vlaams Frites, t

name: Les Caves Populaires
desc: A major bobo hangout, this one specialises in wine as opposed to the more beer-oriented Lush.

name: Lush
desc: Grungy atmosphere and a well thought out selection of beers and tunes have made this a popular space with the bobo crowd. There's not much in the way of furniture, so it's standing room only when the place gets hopping.

name: Carette
desc: This Pâtisserie and Salon de thé also has great food. The salads are amazing, and there are delicious cakes for dessert.

name: La Gare Chaussée De La Muette
Le Malakoff
desc: Just take the menu of the day

name: Le Coq
desc: A hip and trendy modern brasserie where the 16th arrondissement's posh population meets

name: Café Brassac
desc: Very nice cafe with good lunch and dinner. Lots of people go their for business lunch

name: L'Astrance
desc: 3 Michelin stars. Considered one of the best restaurants of Paris. Do not go there, if you are hungry and want to get full.

name: Café de l'Homme

name: La Can Tinh
desc: Vietnamese restaurant.

name: Quinte & Sens
desc: Under the direction of chef Jean-Paul Corbillet, the Quinte & Sens offers modern cuisine, including two-course "power lunches" for €29.

name: Apogé
desc: Apogé is a dynamic, all-in-one stop for French wine. Part bar, part merchant, part oenology school, its passionate, friendly founders are happy to share their expert advice. Not only are over 100 wines available by the g

name: Mé Miam
desc: Cheap and small Vietnamese takeaway selling Banh Mi and Bo Bun.

name: Le Girafon
desc: Pizzeria (oh I'm sorry, "Franco-Italian restaurant") with some interesting French interpretations.

name: Quai Ouest x Bocca sur Seine
desc: Expensive French/Mediterranean restaurant.

name: Péniche Mangareva
desc: Eclectic restaurant, offering combined food, hammam and massage packages for up to €112.

name: Le Comptoir Saint-Cloud
desc: Popular French bistro with outdoor terrace.

name: Bureaux de la Colline
desc: This 1970s office block has various sandwich shops for a quick lunch.

name: Lovebird Saint-Cloud
desc: Very nice restaurant, tapas and cocktails bar. Home-made cuisine based on fresh products, Astro cocktails creations.

name: YOLO Suresnes
desc: Homemade plates and vegetarian dishes made with fresh product, and brunch on Sundays by reservation. Bar, coffee shop with creative cocktails, happy hour and terrace.

name: Le Beauharnais
desc: It has a very beautiful view on the Saint-Pierre Saint-Paul church

name: L'Auberge du Fruit Défendu
desc: Also a hostel.

name: La Terrasse
desc: Traditional French dishes.
